article_content: (CNN) -- A 47-year-old man from Northern Ireland was found not guilty on Friday of the murder of two British soldiers in the 2009 killings at an army base in Northern Ireland. Brian Shivers had been accused of killing Patrick Azimkar, 21, and Mark Quinsey, 23, two English soldiers who were gunned down outside Massereene Barracks. The off-duty and unarmed servicemen were ambushed with gunfire as they collected a pizza delivery at the front gate of the base, hours before they were due to leave for a tour of Afghanistan. They were the first members of the British security forces to be killed in Northern Ireland since the signing of the Good Friday peace agreement in 1998. The Real IRA, a splinter group of the Irish Republican Army, claimed responsibility for the attack. Shivers had been convicted of the murders last year and ordered to serve at least 25 years in jail. The Northern Ireland Court of Appeal quashed that judgment this year after Shivers challenged the trial verdict. He was then ordered to face a retrial. Prosecutors said Shivers' DNA was found on matchsticks and a mobile phone found in and around an abandoned getaway car. The defense argued that the DNA did not prove he was involved in the shooting and could have been innocently associated with people who used the car. Shivers' attorney described him as an 'unlikely terrorist' because he had cystic fibrosis and a doctor had told him he only had a few years to live. The judge effectively sided with the defense, stating that the evidence wasn't strong enough. Another man, Colin Duffy, had been acquitted last year. Shivers was also acquitted of attempting to kill four other soldiers and two pizza delivery men and of torching a getaway car.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Seorang pria berusia 47 tahun dari Irlandia Utara dinyatakan tidak bersalah pada hari Jumat atas pembunuhan dua tentara Inggris dalam pembunuhan tahun 2009 di pangkalan tentara di Irlandia Utara. Brian Shivers didakwa membunuh Patrick Azimkar, 21, dan Mark Quinsey, 23, dua tentara Inggris yang ditembak mati di luar Massereene Barracks. Para prajurit yang sedang istirahat dan tidak bersenjata disergap dengan tembakan saat mereka mengambil pengiriman pizza di gerbang depan pangkalan, beberapa jam sebelum mereka harus berangkat untuk tur ke Afghanistan. Mereka adalah anggota pertama keamanan Inggris yang terbunuh di Irlandia Utara sejak penandatanganan perjanjian perdamaian Jumat Agung pada tahun 1998. Real IRA, kelompok pemisah dari Irish Republican Army, mengaku bertanggung jawab atas serangan itu. Shivers telah dihukum atas pembunuhan tersebut tahun lalu dan diperintahkan menjalani hukuman penjara selama 25 tahun. Pengadilan Banding Irlandia Utara membatalkan putusan tersebut setelah Shivers mempertanyakan keputusan persidangan. Dia kemudian diperintahkan menghadapi persidangan ulang. Jaksa penuntut mengatakan DNA Shivers ditemukan pada korek api dan ponsel yang ditemukan di sekitar mobil pelarian yang ditinggalkan. Pembelaan berpendapat bahwa DNA tersebut tidak membuktikan dia terlibat dalam penembakan dan mungkin secara tidak sengaja terkait dengan orang-orang yang menggunakan mobil itu. Pengacara Shivers menggambarkannya sebagai 'teroris yang tidak mungkin' karena dia memiliki fibrosis kistik dan seorang dokter telah memberi tahu dia bahwa dia hanya memiliki beberapa tahun untuk hidup. Hakim secara efektif berpihak pada pembelaan, menyatakan bahwa bukti tidak cukup kuat. Seorang pria lain, Colin Duffy, telah dibebaskan tahun lalu. Shivers juga dibebaskan dari upaya membunuh empat tentara lainnya dan dua pengirim pizza serta membakar mobil pelarian.

article_content: By Rebecca Camber. UPDATED: 11:41 EST, 24 January 2012. On trial: Asil Nadir arrives at the Old Bailey, London, with his wife, Nur. It has been nearly 19 years since he famously fled British justice. But yesterday Asil Nadir finally went on trial for allegedly stealing £150 million to fund his luxury lifestyle. The 70-year-old is accused of plundering his Polly Peck business empire to pay for lavish properties, cars, and gifts for himself and his family, causing the firm to collapse nearly 22 years ago. The tycoon, who had at his disposal five company cars including Bentleys and a Ferrari Testarossa, as well as a company aeroplane, then fled as fraud investigators closed in. On the eve of his trial in May 1993, he jetted off to his native Northern Cyprus where he set up home. It was not until August 2010 that Nadir flew back to London and was re-arrested. Yesterday the former fugitive entered the Old Bailey grinning as he prepared to go into the dock for the first time to face 13 charges of theft. Nadir stopped to shake hands and wave at supporters after arriving in a presidential-style cavalcade. He was flanked by minders and accompanied by his glamorous second wife Nur, 27. The defendant sat calmly as the court heard how he raided the firm's accounts to splash out on a string of million-pound properties and luxuries such as a new Mercedes for his first wife Ayshegul, cash for his son Birol, and livestock for a 'model farm' on a country estate in Leicestershire. He even used the stolen cash to pay off his tax bill and debts, it was alleged. Nadir is facing trial over 13 specimen counts of theft amounting to £33 million and $2.5 million. But prosecutor Philip Shears, QC, said the 'much bigger picture' was that he stole £146 million and $6.4 million in a total of 64 transfers. The cash was allegedly taken between August 1987 and August 1990 from three accounts held by Polly Peck International (PPI), a major international conglomerate which had more than 200 subsidiaries trading in food, electronics, textiles, and leisure and housed the Del Monte fruit business. Nadir is said to have ordered his henchmen to take out bags of bank notes, often totaling £100,000, from banks which he 'dishonestly routed away to benefit himself, his family, or associates'. Mr. Shears told jurors: 'Mr. Nadir was chairman and chief executive of PPI. He was a man who wielded very considerable power over its operations and management and that of its subsidiaries, particularly in Northern Cyprus. In the dock: A court drawing shows Nadir on the opening day of his trial, where the Old Bailey heard he stole £150 million from his business empire. 'Dishonest': Nadir and his wife Nur at court, where Nadir is on trial over allegations he stole £34 million. 'We say he abused that power and helped himself to tens of millions of pounds of PPI's money. 'The time span of the counts is between 1987 and 1990. That is a long time ago. Why are we trying matters so long ago? The answer is simple. He was due to stand his trial in late 1993 but in May of 1993, he fled the country to Northern Cyprus, thus leaving the jurisdiction, only to return in August 2010. 'The funds were used in a variety of ways for the benefit of Nadir himself, his family, and his associates.' Exit: Nadir leaves court this evening following the conclusion of the day's proceedings at the Old Bailey. The jury heard that Nadir hid £7.5 million he siphoned off from his firm in his mother, Safiye's, bank accounts. The rest of the stolen cash went through a complex series of transactions through companies in Switzerland and the Bahamas and a bank he owned in Northern Cyprus, it was said. When the company folded owing more than £550 million, administrators found that the vast majority of cash was held in Northern Cyprus. By December 1989, £202.6 million – 81 percent of all Polly Peck's cash balances – was held by its Turkish and Northern Cyprus companies. By the end of June 1990, this had risen to £305.8 million. When questioned about the cash transfers, Nadir allegedly told his board it made good business sense and that he needed to pay citrus growers for produce. Shortly before the firm collapsed in October 1990, Nadir increased his salary from £200,000 to £350,000, the court heard. Mr. Shears said: 'When the administrators went to Northern Cyprus they effectively found no cash at all, just a black hole. We say there is a perfectly good explanation for that – it had gone. Mr. Nadir had stolen it.' The jury heard that Nadir was the dominant force in the company which he built up from an ailing textiles firm in the early 1980s. Mr. Shears said: 'He directed its affairs in an autocratic manner and refused to tolerate rival sources of power in the management or to accept constraints upon his freedom of action.' Unlike other businesses, PPI operated with a single signatory system where only one member of the board could authorize the transfer of funds as Nadir refused to 'surrender the power to transfer funds'. But he relied on help from his alleged accomplice, Elizabeth Forsyth, his 'personal financial officer' who was managing director of South Audley Management (SAM) which ran most of the money transactions. Jason Davies, another director of SAM, also 'provided assistance to Nadir in his dishonest enterprise', the court heard. They allegedly worked together to help Nadir use PPI money to secretly buy £26.2 million in PPI shares to prop up its share price, which allowed the company to borrow more from banks, helped maintain the value of Nadir's own shareholding, and prevented lenders from forcing the sale of his personal stock. The court heard that Nadir also used the cash to invest in businesses he owned or controlled. They included a newspaper and publishing company in Northern Cyprus, a Swiss computer firm he used to get a Swiss residence permit, a Turkish airline, Baggrave Farm – a country estate in Leicestershire – and Burley on the Hill, a hotel development project in Rutland. Nadir, of Belgravia, denies 13 counts of theft. The trial continues.
translated_content: Oleh Rebecca Camber. DIKEMAS KINI: 11:41 EST, 24 Januari 2012. Dalam persidangan: Asil Nadir tiba di Old Bailey, London, bersama istrinya, Nur. Telah hampir 19 tahun sejak dia terkenal melarikan diri dari keadilan Inggris. Tetapi kemarin Asil Nadir akhirnya menghadapi persidangan atas tuduhan mencuri £150 juta untuk membiayai gaya hidup mewahnya. Pengusaha berusia 70 tahun itu didakwa merampas kekayaannya sendiri dari konglomerasi bisnis Polly Peck untuk membeli properti dan mobil mewah serta hadiah untuk dirinya sendiri dan keluarganya, yang menyebabkan keruntuhan perusahaan itu hampir 22 tahun yang lalu. Tokoh yang memiliki lima mobil perusahaan termasuk Bentley dan Ferrari Testarossa, serta pesawat perusahaan, kemudian melarikan diri ketika penyelidik penipuan mendekat. Pada malam sebelum persidangannya pada Mei 1993, dia terbang ke Cyprus Utara tempat kelahirannya dan mendirikan rumah. Baru pada Agustus 2010 Nadir kembali ke London dan ditangkap kembali. Kemarin mantan pelarian itu masuk ke Old Bailey tersenyum saat bersiap masuk ke bangku terdakwa untuk pertama kalinya menghadapi 13 tuduhan pencurian. Nadir berhenti untuk berjabat tangan dan mengacungkan jari setelah tiba dalam kavaleri gaya presiden. Dia dikelilingi oleh penjaga dan didampingi oleh istri keduanya yang glamor, Nur, 27 tahun. Terpidana itu duduk tenang saat pengadilan mendengar bagaimana dia merampas akun perusahaan untuk membelanjakan uang jutaan poundsterling untuk properti dan kemewahan seperti Mercedes baru untuk istri pertamanya Ayshegul, uang untuk putranya Birol, dan ternak untuk 'peternakan model' di lahan di Leicestershire. Dia bahkan menggunakan uang curian untuk membayar tagihan pajak dan utangnya, demikian didakwa. Nadir menghadapi persidangan atas 13 tuduhan pencurian sebesar £33 juta dan $2,5 juta. Tetapi jaksa Philip Shears, QC, mengatakan 'gambaran yang jauh lebih besar' adalah bahwa dia mencuri £146 juta dan $6,4 juta dalam total 64 transfer. Uang itu didakwa diambil antara Agustus 1987 dan Agustus 1990 dari tiga akun yang dipegang oleh Polly Peck International (PPI), konglomerasi internasional besar yang memiliki lebih dari 200 anak perusahaan yang bergerak dalam makanan, elektronik, tekstil, dan hiburan serta menaungi bisnis buah Del Monte. Nadir didakwa memerintahkan antek-anteknya untuk mengambil tas-tas uang dari bank, seringkali senilai £100.000, yang dia 'salurkan secara tidak jujur untuk kepentingannya sendiri, keluarganya, atau rekan-rekannya'. Mr. Shears berkata kepada juri: 'Mr. Nadir adalah ketua dan CEO PPI. Dia adalah orang yang memegang kekuasaan yang sangat besar atas operasinya dan manajemen serta anak perusahaannya, terutama di Cyprus Utara. Di bangku terdakwa: Sebuah gambar pengadilan menunjukkan Nadir pada hari pembukaan persidangannya, di mana Old Bailey mendengar dia mencuri £150 juta dari kekaisaran bisnisnya. 'Tidak jujur': Nadir dan istrinya Nur di pengadilan, di mana Nadir diadili atas tuduhan mencuri £34 juta. 'Kami mengatakan dia salah gunakan kekuasaan itu dan membantu dirinya sendiri dengan puluhan juta poundsterling uang PPI. 'Rentang waktu tuduhan itu antara 1987 dan 1990. Itu sudah lama. Mengapa kita mengadili masalah yang sudah lama? Jawabannya sederhana. Dia seharusnya menghadapi persidangan pada akhir 1993 tetapi pada Mei 1993 dia melarikan diri dari negara ke Cyprus Utara, meninggalkan yurisdiksi, hanya untuk kembali pada Agustus 2010. 'Dana digunakan dalam berbagai cara untuk kepentingan Nadir sendiri, keluarganya, dan rekan-rekannya.' Keluar: Nadir meninggalkan pengadilan pada malam ini setelah selesainya sidang hari ini di Old Bailey. Juri mendengar bahwa Nadir menyembunyikan £7,5 juta yang dia salurkan dari perusahaannya di akun bank ibunya, Safiye. Sisa uang curian melalui serangkaian transaksi kompleks melalui perusahaan di Swiss dan Bahama serta bank yang dia miliki di Cyprus Utara, demikian dikatakan. Ketika perusahaan bubar dengan utang lebih dari £550 juta, administrator menemukan bahwa sebagian besar uang disimpan di Cyprus Utara. Pada Desember 1989, £202,6 juta - 81 persen dari semua saldo uang Polly Peck - dipegang oleh perusahaannya di Turki dan Cyprus Utara. Pada akhir Juni 1990 ini meningkat menjadi £305,8 juta. Ketika ditanya tentang transfer uang, Nadir didakwa memberi tahu dewan direksinya itu adalah keputusan bisnis yang baik dan bahwa dia perlu membayar petani jeruk buah untuk produknya. Mendekati kebangkrutan perusahaan itu pada Oktober 1990, Nadir menaikkan gajinya dari £200.000 menjadi £350.000, demikian didengar pengadilan. Mr. Shears berkata: 'Ketika administrator pergi ke Cyprus Utara mereka tidak menemukan uang sama sekali, hanya lubang hitam. Kami mengatakan ada penjelasan yang sangat baik untuk itu - itu telah hilang. Mr. Nadir telah mencurinya.' Juri mendengar bahwa Nadir adalah kekuatan dominan dalam perusahaan yang dia bangun dari perusahaan tekstil yang goyah pada awal 1980-an. Mr. Shears berkata: 'Dia mengarahkan urusannya dengan cara otoriter dan menolak untuk menerima sumber-sumber kekuasaan saingan dalam manajemen atau membatasi kebebasan bertindaknya. 'Berbeda dengan bisnis lain, PPI beroperasi dengan sistem penandatangan tunggal di mana hanya satu anggota dewan dapat mengotorisasi transfer dana karena Nadir menolak 'menyerahkan kekuasaan untuk mentransfer dana'. Tetapi dia bergantung pada bantuan pembantunya yang diduga, Elizabeth Forsyth, 'pejabat keuangan pribadinya' yang merupakan direktur manajer South Audley Management (SAM) yang menjalankan sebagian besar transaksi uang. Jason Davies, direktur lain dari SAM, juga 'memberikan bantuan kepada Nadir dalam perusahaan curangnya', demikian didengar pengadilan. Mereka didakwa bekerja sama untuk membantu Nadir menggunakan uang PPI untuk secara diam-diam membeli saham PPI senilai £26,2 juta untuk memperkuat harga sahamnya, yang memungkinkan perusahaan meminjam lebih banyak dari bank, membantu mempertahankan nilai kepemilikan saham Nadir sendiri, dan mencegah para peminjam memaksa penjualan saham pribadinya. Pengadilan mendengar bahwa Nadir juga menggunakan uang itu untuk berinvestasi pada bisnis yang dia miliki atau kendalikan. Mereka termasuk perusahaan surat kabar dan penerbitan di Cyprus Utara, perusahaan komputer Swiss yang dia gunakan untuk mendapatkan izin tinggal di Swiss, maskapai penerbangan Turki, Baggrave Farm - sebuah lahan di Leicestershire - dan Burley on the Hill, sebuah proyek pengembangan hotel di Rutland. Nadir, dari Belgravia, membantah 13 tuduhan pencurian. Persidangan berlanjut.

article_content: Ravel Morrison has been instructed to depart from West Ham following his involvement of the PFA to address a disagreement over his weekly earnings of £15,000. The problematic attacker is continually penalized by the club for bad behavior and has been urged to secure a new team during the upcoming January transfer period. Morrison, who is 21 years old, is backed by the PFA in his dispute with West Ham, although the club maintains that they have adhered to their internal disciplinary guidelines for players. Morrison had an early return from his loan at Cardiff City and has been directed to leave West Ham. After a disheartening 5-0 loss to Nottingham Forest in January 2014, Morrison shared a picture of himself wearing West Ham United training gear during a workout session on Instagram. The former Manchester United player has been reassigned to practice with the Under 21 development group as the situation persists. He hasn't featured in a match for West Ham since their 3-1 loss to Southampton at Upton Park on August 31. Despite being loaned out to teams like Birmingham, QPR, and most recently Cardiff to aid his progress, Morrison has struggled to meet expectations. Recognizing his talent, Sam Allardyce, the manager of West Ham, has been unable to fully utilize Morrison's abilities since his arrival from Manchester United in 2012. Known for his disruptive behavior, Allardyce believed he could manage the England Under 21 player. However, Morrison is now searching for a new club but refuses to leave until his wage issues with West Ham are settled by the PFA. Additionally, Morrison is facing a court case starting on January 26 regarding accusations of assaulting his girlfriend and her mother in July of the previous year. In February 2011, Morrison was given a 12-month referral order for threatening a mugging victim to prevent them from testifying. In May 2011, he appeared in court for allegedly attacking his girlfriend, though the charges were later dismissed. On January 31, 2012, Morrison joined West Ham from Manchester United, with Sir Alex Ferguson praising his exceptional football skills. In February 2012, Morrison was fined £7,000 by the Football Association for homophobic comments on Twitter. In September 2012, while on loan at Birmingham City, his poor attitude during training led the team's manager to consider ending his loan. Eventually, he regained his spot and became a valuable team member. In July 2014, Morrison was detained for allegedly assaulting his ex-girlfriend and her mother. In November 2014, he was acquitted of threatening to throw acid at his ex-girlfriend.

Pada Februari 2012, Morrison didenda £7,000 oleh Asosiasi Sepak Bola karena komentar homofobik di Twitter. Pada September 2012, saat dipinjamkan ke Birmingham City, sikap buruknya selama latihan membuat manajer tim mempertimbangkan untuk mengakhiri pinjamannya. Akhirnya, dia merebut kembali tempatnya dan menjadi anggota tim yang berharga. Pada Juli 2014, Morrison ditahan karena didakwa menyerang mantan pacarnya dan ibunya. Pada November 2014, dia dibebaskan dari tuduhan mengancam melemparkan asam ke wajah mantan pacarnya.

article_content: Lewis Hamilton expressed that it 'felt amazing' to be part of the team that secured Mercedes' first-ever constructors' title. The 29-year-old British driver won the Russian Grand Prix in Sochi, with his teammate and championship rival Nico Rosberg finishing second, dethroning Red Bull. After receiving his race trophy from Russian President Vladimir Putin, Hamilton shared his pride in contributing to this historic achievement. Mercedes co-team boss Paddy Lowe joined Hamilton and Rosberg on the podium to celebrate the victory. Reflecting on the win, Hamilton said, 'It's history, so we're proud to be a part of it. It's amazing, it's a beautiful day.' Over the radio, he congratulated the team: 'Congratulations to the team on winning the constructors' championship. Great job man! History in the making!' Rosberg admitted his mistake on the first lap of the inaugural Grand Prix, which effectively handed the race win to Hamilton. Despite his disappointment, Rosberg acknowledged the team's deserving victory, stating, 'Half of me is extremely disappointed, but I'm also really really happy because everyone in the team deserves it so much. It's their most important title, so I can smile a bit.'

Setelah menerima piala balap dari Presiden Rusia Vladimir Putin, Hamilton membagikan kebanggaannya atas kontribusinya pada pencapaian sejarah ini. Bos co-tim Mercedes Paddy Lowe bergabung dengan Hamilton dan Rosberg di podium untuk merayakan kemenangan. Merenungkan kemenangan, Hamilton berkata, 'Ini sejarah, jadi kami bangga menjadi bagian dari itu. Ini luar biasa, ini hari yang indah.' Rosberg mengakui kesalahannya di putaran pertama Grand Prix perdana, yang secara efektif memberikan kemenangan balap kepada Hamilton. Meski kecewa, Rosberg mengakui kemenangan tim yang layak, dengan mengatakan, 'Separuh dari saya sangat kecewa, tapi saya juga sangat senang karena semua orang dalam tim layak mendapatkannya. Ini gelar paling penting mereka, jadi saya bisa tersenyum sedikit.'

article_content: Four bronze angels, originally created for Cardinal Wolsey's tomb but lost for nearly 500 years, are being bought for the nation at a price of £2.8 million. These opulent, metre-high statues were made for Henry VIII's chief adviser in 1524 but disappeared after he fell out of the king's favor, at one point adorning the gateposts of a country manor. The popularity of the BBC drama 'Wolf Hall,' based on Hilary Mantel's double Booker Prize-winning book series, has helped bring these sculptures into the spotlight and raised £90,000 from the public. Preserved: Originally designed for Cardinal Wolsey's tomb, these bronze angels will be permanently preserved in the Victoria & Albert Museum in London after the museum raised £2.8 million to buy them for the nation. Piece of history: Nearly £90,000 of the money came from the public, including the sale of 33,000 pin badges for £1 each in the museum shop. Wolsey fell out of favor with Henry VIII, and his tomb was never finished. London's Victoria & Albert Museum has raised £2.8 million in total to acquire the works, led by a £2 million grant from the National Heritage Memorial Fund. The Art Fund contributed another £500,000, the Friends of the V&A gave £200,000, and of the public fundraising, £33,000 came from the sale of 'Save The Wolsey Angels' badges in the museum shop. V&A director Martin Roth said: 'The Wolsey Angels are a vital part of our national history and artistic heritage. We are very grateful to everyone who contributed to our fundraising appeal to ensure these outstanding sculptures, which were thought to be lost, are reunited and preserved at the V&A for future generations.' Drama: The campaign was given a boost by 'Wolf Hall,' in which Wolsey is played by Jonathan Pryce. Played by Jonathan Pryce in the BBC adaptation of 'Wolf Hall,' Cardinal Thomas Wolsey amassed considerable power in the early 1500s as one of Henry VIII's closest confidantes. But the pair fell out after the king's infamous attempt to annul his marriage with his first wife, Catherine of Aragon, because she had not produced a healthy son. Cardinal Wolsey appealed for an annulment to the Pope, based partly on the claim that Catherine was not a virgin when she married Henry—a claim she denied. Caught in an international deadlock between Henry and Catherine's powerful nephew, the Holy Roman Emperor Charles V, the Pope delayed the decision, and Wolsey was stripped of many of his offices in 1529. He died just a year later mid-way through a journey to London, where he was due to face accusations of treason. Work on the angels had already started six years earlier in 1524, but the magnificent Renaissance-style tomb Wolsey had planned would never be erected. The four bronzes were commissioned from the Florentine sculptor Benedetto da Rovezzano, who made them between 1524 and 1529. Along with the rest of Wolsey's possessions and his planned tomb, the angels were appropriated by Henry VIII, who intended to use them for himself. Benedetto was commissioned to complete the tomb and established himself at Westminster, where he employed founders and other craftsmen. However, progress was halting, and Henry VIII did not see the tomb finished. Each of Henry VIII's three children expressed the intention to complete the memorial after he died, but they also failed to do so. Battle: The Cardinal fell out with Henry VIII (played in the BBC drama by Damian Lewis) after he failed to persuade the Pope to annul the king's marriage so he could marry Anne Boleyn (played by Claire Foy). Shifting power: Mark Rylance as Thomas Cromwell and Claire Foy as Anne Boleyn in the BBC adaptation. Elizabeth I moved the parts of the tomb to Windsor in 1565, where they stayed for 80 years until parts were sold to raise money during the Civil War. Only a black stone chest—which now houses Lord Nelson's remains at St. Paul's Cathedral—was known to have survived until two of the angels appeared at auction in 1994. Unillustrated and cataloged only as 'in Italian Renaissance style,' they were acquired by a Parisian art dealer, and later the Italian scholar Francesco Caglioti attributed them to Benedetto. The other two angels were discovered in 2008 at Great Harrowden Hall, Northamptonshire—where all four had once perched atop the country manor's magnificent gateposts. During the fundraising campaign, all four unevenly weathered angels were reunited for the first time since 1988 in the V&A's Medieval & Renaissance Galleries. They remain there and will now stay in the museum, where they will be conserved and made to look as similar as they did in the day of Henry VIII. Unlikely home: The four statues once stood upon the gateposts at Great Harrowden Hall in Northamptonshire. New home: They will now be preserved for the nation at the Victoria & Albert Museum in central London. Fiona Talbott, head of the National Heritage Memorial Fund, said: 'Many of us have been enjoying the BBC's production of 'Wolf Hall,' which makes it even more fitting to celebrate the purchase of these extraordinary statues. Congratulations to the V&A for being so tenacious in securing their future. We feel proud to have played a part too and hope that the Cardinal Wolsey's Angels—thanks to their current high profile—will attract many admirers both now and in the future.'
translated_content: Empat patung perunggu malaikat, yang awalnya dibuat untuk makam Kardinal Wolsey tetapi hilang selama hampir 500 tahun, sedang dibeli untuk bangsa dengan harga £2.8 juta. Patung-patung mewah setinggi satu meter ini dibuat untuk penasihat utama Henry VIII pada tahun 1524 tetapi menghilang setelah dia kehilangan kepercayaan raja, pada suatu waktu menghiasi tiang gerbang sebuah rumah desa. Popularitas drama BBC 'Wolf Hall,' yang didasarkan pada seri buku pemenang dua kali Booker Prize karya Hilary Mantel, telah membantu membawa patung-patung ini ke sorotan dan mengumpulkan £90,000 dari masyarakat. Terpelihara: Dirancang awalnya untuk makam Kardinal Wolsey, patung-patung perunggu ini akan dijaga secara permanen di Museum Victoria & Albert di London setelah museum mengumpulkan £2.8 juta untuk membelinya untuk bangsa. Sejarah: Hampir £90,000 dari uang tersebut berasal dari masyarakat, termasuk penjualan 33,000 pin badge seharga £1 masing-masing di toko museum. Wolsey kehilangan kepercayaan Henry VIII, dan makamnya tidak pernah selesai. Museum Victoria & Albert di London telah mengumpulkan total £2.8 juta untuk memperoleh karya-karya tersebut, dipimpin oleh hibah sebesar £2 juta dari National Heritage Memorial Fund. The Art Fund menyumbang £500,000 lainnya, Friends of the V&A memberikan £200,000, dan dari penggalangan dana masyarakat, £33,000 berasal dari penjualan pin 'Save The Wolsey Angels' di toko museum. Direktur V&A Martin Roth berkata: 'Wolsey Angels adalah bagian vital dari sejarah nasional dan warisan artistik kami. Kami sangat berterima kasih kepada semua yang berkontribusi pada kampanye penggalangan dana kami untuk memastikan patung-patung luar biasa ini, yang dianggap hilang, bersatu kembali dan dijaga di V&A untuk generasi mendatang.' Drama: Kampanye ini mendapat dorongan dari 'Wolf Hall,' di mana Wolsey diperankan oleh Jonathan Pryce. Dalam adaptasi BBC dari 'Wolf Hall,' Kardinal Thomas Wolsey mengumpulkan kekuasaan yang signifikan pada awal 1500-an sebagai salah satu orang kepercayaan terdekat Henry VIII. Tetapi mereka berpisah setelah upaya terkenal raja untuk membatalkan pernikahannya dengan istri pertamanya, Catherine of Aragon, karena dia tidak melahirkan putra sehat. Kardinal Wolsey mengajukan banding ke Paus untuk pembatalan, didasarkan sebagian pada klaim bahwa Catherine bukan perawan ketika dia menikah dengan Henry—sebuah klaim yang dia ngeri. Terjebak dalam kebuntuan internasional antara Henry dan keponakan Catherine yang kuat, Kaisar Romawi Suci Charles V, Paus menunda keputusan, dan Wolsey dicabut dari banyak jabatannya pada tahun 1529. Dia meninggal setahun kemudian tengah perjalanan ke London, di mana dia akan menghadapi tuduhan pengkhianatan. Pekerjaan pada patung-patung malaikat sudah dimulai enam tahun sebelumnya pada tahun 1524, tetapi makam gaya Renaisans yang megah yang direncanakan Wolsey tidak akan pernah didirikan. Empat patung perunggu tersebut dipesan dari pemahat Florentine Benedetto da Rovezzano, yang membuatnya antara tahun 1524 dan 1529. Bersama dengan sisa harta benda Wolsey dan makam yang direncanakannya, patung-patung malaikat disita oleh Henry VIII yang berniat menggunakannya untuk dirinya sendiri. Benedetto diberi tugas menyelesaikan makam dan menetap di Westminster, di mana dia mempekerjakan pencetak logam dan pengrajin lainnya. Namun, kemajuan berjalan lambat, dan Henry VIII tidak melihat makam selesai. Setiap anak Henry VIII mengungkapkan niat untuk menyelesaikan monumen setelah dia meninggal, tetapi mereka juga gagal melakukannya. Pertempuran: Kardinal berpisah dengan Henry VIII (diperankan dalam drama BBC oleh Damian Lewis) setelah dia gagal membujuk Paus untuk membatalkan pernikahan raja agar dia bisa menikahi Anne Boleyn (diperankan oleh Claire Foy). Pergeseran kekuasaan: Mark Rylance sebagai Thomas Cromwell dan Claire Foy sebagai Anne Boleyn dalam adaptasi BBC. Elizabeth I memindahkan bagian-bagian makam ke Windsor pada tahun 1565, di mana mereka tinggal selama 80 tahun hingga bagian-bagian tersebut dijual untuk mengumpulkan uang selama Perang Saudara. Hanya peti batu hitam—yang sekarang menampung jenazah Lord Nelson di St. Paul's Cathedral—yang diketahui selamat hingga dua patung malaikat muncul di lelang pada tahun 1994. Tidak diilustrasikan dan hanya dikatalogkan sebagai 'gaya Renaisans Italia,' mereka diperoleh oleh seorang pedagang seni Paris, dan kemudian sarjana Italia Francesco Caglioti mengaitkannya dengan Benedetto. Dua patung malaikat lainnya ditemukan pada tahun 2008 di Great Harrowden Hall, Northamptonshire—di mana semua empat pernah berdiri di atas tiang gerbang megah rumah desa. Selama kampanye penggalangan dana, empat patung malaikat yang cuaca tidak merata bersatu kembali untuk pertama kalinya sejak tahun 1988 di Galeri Abad Pertengahan & Renaisans V&A. Mereka tetap di sana dan sekarang akan tinggal di museum, di mana mereka akan dikonservasi dan dibuat agar terlihat seperti pada zaman Henry VIII. Rumah yang tidak mungkin: Empat patung pernah berdiri di atas tiang gerbang di Great Harrowden Hall di Northamptonshire. Rumah baru: Mereka sekarang akan dijaga untuk bangsa di Museum Victoria & Albert di pusat London. Fiona Talbott, kepala National Heritage Memorial Fund, berkata: 'Banyak di antara kita telah menikmati produksi BBC dari 'Wolf Hall,' yang membuatnya lebih tepat untuk merayakan pembelian patung-patung luar biasa ini. Selamat untuk V&A yang begitu gigih dalam memastikan masa depan mereka. Kami merasa bangga bisa ikut berkontribusi dan berharap bahwa Malaikat Kardinal Wolsey—karena profil tinggi mereka saat ini—akan menarik banyak pengagum baik sekarang maupun di masa depan.'

article_content: Andrew Tahmooressi, a Marine veteran, is currently detained in a Mexican jail for carrying illegal firearms across the border on March 31. Tahmooressi insists that his arrest was a misunderstanding, claiming he made a wrong turn and ended up in Mexico with guns that were legally purchased in the United States. His mother, Jill Tahmooressi, agrees that her son should be freed and allowed to return to San Diego. Tahmooressi, who served two tours in Afghanistan before being honorably discharged, explained to Mexican authorities that he had no intention of smuggling weapons. He reported feeling threatened while in custody. His mother revealed that he had moved to the west coast specifically to seek treatment for Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Nearly two dozen U.S. lawmakers have written to the Mexican government urging Tahmooressi’s swift release, but their pleas have so far gone unanswered. Protesters have also gathered in front of the Mexican consulate in Miami, calling for his freedom. Despite the challenges, Tahmooressi remains hopeful and maintains his innocence, putting his faith in God. Jill Tahmooressi continues to hope for her son’s release, either before or shortly after his next court hearing scheduled for May 28.
translated_content: Andrew Tahmooressi, seorang veteran Marinir, saat ini ditahan di penjara Meksiko karena membawa senjata api ilegal melintasi perbatasan pada 31 Maret. Tahmooressi berpendapat bahwa penangkapannya adalah kesalahpahaman, dengan mengklaim dia salah belok dan berakhir di Meksiko dengan senjata yang secara legal dibeli di Amerika Serikat. Ibunya, Jill Tahmooressi, setuju bahwa putranya harus dibebaskan dan diizinkan kembali ke San Diego. Tahmooressi, yang telah bertugas dua kali di Afghanistan sebelum diberhentikan dengan hormat, menjelaskan kepada pejabat Meksiko bahwa dia tidak berniat menyelundupkan senjata. Dia melaporkan merasa terancam selama tahanan. Ibunya mengungkapkan bahwa dia pindah ke pantai barat khususnya untuk mencari perawatan Gangguan Stres Pasca-Trauma (PTSD). Hampir dua dozen pembuat undang-undang AS telah menulis kepada pemerintah Meksiko memohon pembebasan cepat Tahmooressi, tetapi permohonan mereka belum mendapat respons. Pengunjuk rasa juga berkumpul di depan konsulat Meksiko di Miami, meminta kebebasannya. Meski tantangan, Tahmooressi tetap percaya diri dan mempertahankan ketidakbersalahannya, meletakkan kepercayaannya pada Tuhan. Jill Tahmooressi terus berharap putranya dibebaskan, baik sebelum atau tidak lama setelah sidang berikutnya yang dijadwalkan pada 28 Mei.

article_content: In a dramatic turn of events, Peter Chan Chun-chuen, once a close confidant and feng shui advisor to one of Asia's richest women, has been sentenced to 12 years in prison. Chan, previously known as Tony Chan, was found guilty of fabricating a will that would have granted him Nina Wang's massive fortune. The lengthy legal battle captivated Hong Kong, culminating in a guilty verdict handed down by a jury last Friday. Justice Andrew Macrae, in his sentencing remarks, noted that Chan displayed 'not the slightest remorse' for his actions. Macrae went on to describe Chan as a 'clever and beguiling charlatan,' underscoring the depth of his deception. Wang, famously known for her distinctive pigtail braids and the nickname 'Little Sweetie,' passed away from cancer in 2007. Following her death, Chan presented a will claiming to be her lover and confidant for over 14 years, which designated him as the sole beneficiary of her $4 billion estate. Wang's family contested the will, asserting it was forged. After a protracted legal struggle, the court ruled in 2011 that the estate should go to a charity managed by Wang's siblings, the Chinachem Charitable Foundation Ltd. The trial revealed intricate details about Wang's eccentric lifestyle, her relationship with Chan, and the peculiar feng shui practices she engaged in. Wang was the widow of Hong Kong tycoon Teddy Wang, who vanished after being kidnapped in 1990 and was legally declared dead in 1999. The Wangs' Chinachem Group amassed a fortune through property developments, making them one of Hong Kong's wealthiest families. Chan, a former bartender turned self-taught feng shui master, testified that Wang hired him in 1992 to locate her missing husband. During the trial, it was disclosed that Wang ordered the digging of up to 80 feng shui holes filled with jade on Chinachem Group properties. Feng shui, a traditional Chinese practice, focuses on the arrangement of buildings and objects to harness positive energy. Many corporate structures in Hong Kong are designed according to these principles. The court revealed that Chan received approximately HK$2.1 billion from Wang between 2005 and 2006, which his lawyers argued were payments to prepare him for managing her estate. Recently, Chan has renounced feng shui, converted to Christianity, and changed his name to Peter Chan. It was also revealed that he had 10 prior criminal convictions related to fraudulent credit card applications, for which he was fined HK$20,000 in 1986.
translated_content: Dalam perkembangan dramatis, Peter Chan Chun-chuen, seorang penasihat feng shui dan teman dekat salah satu wanita terkaya di Asia, telah dihukum 12 tahun penjara. Chan, sebelumnya dikenal sebagai Tony Chan, didapati bersalah memalsukan wasiat yang akan memberikannya kekayaan besar Nina Wang. Pertempuran hukum panjang ini membuat Hong Kong terpesona, berpuncak pada vonis bersalah yang dijatuhkan oleh juri pada hari Jumat lalu. Hakim Andrew Macrae, dalam pernyataannya, mencatat bahwa Chan tidak menunjukkan 'sedikit pun penyesalan' atas tindakannya. Macrae kemudian menggambarkan Chan sebagai 'orang yang cerdik dan mempesona,' menekankan kedalaman penipuannya. Wang, yang terkenal dengan ekor kudanya yang unik dan julukan 'Little Sweetie,' meninggal karena kanker pada tahun 2007. Setelah kematiannya, Chan memperlihatkan sebuah wasiat yang mengklaim dirinya sebagai kekasih dan teman dekatnya selama lebih dari 14 tahun, yang menjadikannya satu-satunya pewaris kekayaan senilai $4 miliar. Keluarga Wang mempertanyakan wasiat tersebut, mengklaim bahwa itu palsu. Setelah perjuangan hukum yang panjang, pengadilan memutuskan pada tahun 2011 bahwa warisan harus diserahkan kepada yayasan amal yang dikelola oleh saudara-saudara Wang, Chinachem Charitable Foundation Ltd. Persidangan mengungkapkan detail kompleks tentang gaya hidup eksentrik Wang, hubungannya dengan Chan, dan praktik feng shui yang aneh yang dia lakukan. Wang adalah janda taipan Hong Kong Teddy Wang, yang hilang setelah diculik pada tahun 1990 dan secara hukum dinyatakan meninggal pada tahun 1999. Keluarga Wang, Chinachem Group, mengumpulkan kekayaan melalui pengembangan properti, membuat mereka salah satu keluarga terkaya di Hong Kong. Chan, mantan bartender yang menjadi ahli feng shui mandiri, bersaksi bahwa Wang mempekerjakannya pada tahun 1992 untuk menemukan suaminya yang hilang. Selama persidangan, terungkap bahwa Wang memerintahkan penggalian hingga 80 lubang feng shui yang diisi dengan giok di properti milik Chinachem Group. Feng shui, praktik tradisional Tiongkok, fokus pada susunan bangunan dan objek untuk menghimpun energi positif. Banyak struktur korporasi di Hong Kong dirancang sesuai dengan prinsip-prinsip ini. Pengadilan mengungkapkan bahwa Chan menerima sekitar HK$2.1 miliar dari Wang antara tahun 2005 dan 2006, yang pengacaranya berpendapat merupakan pembayaran untuk mempersiapkannya mengelola kekayaannya. Baru-baru ini, Chan telah meninggalkan feng shui, berpindah agama menjadi Kristen, dan mengubah namanya menjadi Peter Chan. Juga terungkap bahwa dia memiliki 10 kasus pidana sebelumnya terkait dengan pengajuan kartu kredit palsu, untuk yang dia didenda HK$20,000 pada tahun 1986.
post_content: Just in! Peter Chan, ex-lover & feng shui master to billionaire Nina Wang, gets 12 years for forging her will. The dramatic trial revealed eccentric rituals & a complex love affair. #HongKong #CrimeNews #BillionaireDrama

article_content: Manchester United is determined to reject any attempts by Real Madrid to sign Adnan Januzaj. The European champions have included the young Belgian on their summer transfer list, but United insists that the 19-year-old is not for sale at any price, especially after signing him to a long-term contract last winter. It has been a breakthrough season for Januzaj at Old Trafford. He debuted for the team in September and quickly established himself as a key member of the first team. Januzaj is currently away on international duty with Belgium at the World Cup, where he earned his first cap in their final warm-up game against Tunisia in June. Although he was an unused substitute during their 2-1 victory over Algeria in the first game of the competition, he hopes to return to Old Trafford and continue his progression under new manager Louis van Gaal next season.
translated_content: Manchester United bersikeras untuk menolak segala upaya Real Madrid untuk merekrut Adnan Januzaj. Juara Eropa telah memasukkan pemain muda Belgia ini ke dalam daftar transfer musim panas mereka, tetapi United berkeras bahwa pemain berusia 19 tahun itu tidak akan dijual dengan harga apa pun, terutama setelah menandatangani kontrak jangka panjang pada musim dingin lalu. Ini telah menjadi musim penentu bagi Januzaj di Old Trafford. Dia melakukan debut untuk tim pada bulan September dan cepat menjadi anggota kunci dari tim utama. Saat ini, Januzaj sedang bertugas internasional bersama Belgia di Piala Dunia, di mana dia mendapatkan topi pertamanya dalam pertandingan persiapan terakhir mereka melawan Tunisia pada bulan Juni. Meski dia menjadi pemain cadangan yang tidak digunakan selama kemenangan 2-1 atas Aljazair dalam pertandingan pertama kompetisi, dia berharap kembali ke Old Trafford dan melanjutkan perkembangannya di bawah manajer baru Louis van Gaal musim depan.
